description:
Born in 1960 or later? A $1,000 full-retirement-age benefit becomes $700 if you claim at 62 and $1,240 if you wait until 70.

• Claiming at 62 cuts the check by 30% (SSA's own chart)
• Each year you wait past 67 adds 8%, up to age 70
• $1,240 vs $700 is 77% more, every month
• The trade-off: 8 fewer years of checks. On these numbers, break-even is around age 80

Poor health, or need the income now? Claiming earlier can be the right call. Check your own estimate before you choose.
